subject: The place from above — a high vantage before anything happens
reason: The {item} gets the whole place in one frame. Find height first: stairs, a bridge, a rooftop.

subject: Steam off the cup, backlit
reason: Steam only shows against the light. Put the window or the sun behind the cup.

subject: Hands doing one small task — sliding a door, tying a lace, turning a key
reason: Hands carry a sequence without showing a face. Cheap to get, always useful in the edit.

subject: Walking away from camera, through frame
reason: Movement without a face. Lock off and let them walk out of frame — it gives you a clean cut point.

subject: Empty street, leading lines
reason: Early enough and the street is yours. Put the vanishing point on a third.

subject: A texture — stone, weave, grain, rust
reason: The {item} turns a wall into a frame. Side light brings texture out; flat light hides it.

fallback.subject: A texture, as close as the lens will focus
fallback.reason: No macro packed — get as close as it focuses and crop in the edit.

subject: Timelapse — clouds over the skyline
reason: Locked off on the {item}: a 2-second interval for 10 minutes gives you 10 seconds of time passing.

fallback.subject: Timelapse from a wall or a railing
fallback.reason: No tripod — wedge the camera on something solid and don't touch it for ten minutes.

subject: Through a doorway — in on one, out on another
reason: Two doorways shot the same way cut together as one move. Match the framing, not the door.

subject: The scene upside down in a puddle or a window
reason: Get the lens low, almost touching the water. After rain this is free.

subject: A silhouette against the last of the light
reason: Expose for the sky and let them go black. Works at any presence level — nobody is recognisable.

subject: Point of view, walking in
reason: Arrival from your own eyes. Walk slowly and bend your knees — it hides most of the bounce.

subject: Push past something in the foreground to reveal the scene
reason: The {item} makes the push smooth enough to open on. Start close on a plant, a post, a shoulder.

fallback.subject: Pan off something in the foreground to reveal the scene
fallback.reason: No gimbal — a slow pan off a foreground object does the same job.

subject: Rack focus — foreground to background
reason: The {item} opens wide enough for the background to melt. Pull focus slowly — about two seconds.

subject: Signs and their reflections after dark
reason: The {item} holds the shot past dusk without the grain taking over.

subject: Drone pull-back — from the subject out to the whole place
reason: The {item} ends the piece by showing how small it all was. Check the wind and local rules first.

subject: Piece to camera — say where you are and why
reason: The {item} keeps your voice clean over the street. Get two takes, one shorter than you think.

subject: Walk and talk
reason: The {item} stays close to the mouth while you move. Walk slower than feels natural.

subject: A reaction — tasting, seeing, laughing
reason: Reactions are what people remember. Keep rolling after the moment — the real one comes late.

subject: A cutaway of exactly what you're talking about
reason: Every sentence you say to camera needs a picture to cut to. Shoot it straight after, while you remember.

subject: Hero shot of the product on a clean surface
reason: Locked off on the {item} so the product stays sharp and still. Clean the surface — it shows.

fallback.subject: Hero shot of the product, braced on the table edge
fallback.reason: No tripod — rest the camera on the table edge and hold for ten seconds.

subject: The product in someone's hands, being used
reason: Brands want their thing in a life, not on a table. Hands are enough.

subject: Logo or label, close
reason: The {item} gets the label sharp edge to edge. Clients check for this one.

fallback.subject: Logo or label, as close as the lens focuses
fallback.reason: No macro — get as close as it focuses; you'll crop in.

subject: The pour, in slow motion
reason: Your {item} shoots fast enough to slow the pour right down. Light it from behind.

fallback.subject: The pour, real speed, three takes
fallback.reason: No high frame rate — do three pours at real speed and pick the cleanest.

subject: Say the brand's name to camera
reason: Usually contracted, and easy to forget on the day. Say it three ways, with the {item} close.

subject: Interview — main angle, eyeline just off camera
reason: The {item} on them, the camera locked off. Sit them so the window lights one side of the face.

subject: Interview — tighter second angle
reason: The {item} gives you a second size from the same spot, so you can cut mid-answer.

fallback.subject: Interview — reframe tighter between questions
fallback.reason: One lens — reframe tighter between questions and you'll still have a cut point.

subject: Them at work, observed — you're not there
reason: Stay wide and quiet until they forget the camera. Five minutes before you roll is normal.

subject: Their hands at work, close
reason: The {item} gets you close without getting in their way.

fallback.subject: Their hands at work, from beside them
fallback.reason: No long lens — ask if you can stand close for thirty seconds.

subject: A still portrait — they look at the lens for five seconds
reason: Locked off on the {item}. Ask them not to smile. Five seconds feels long; it's the shot people remember.

subject: The outside of where it happens
reason: The audience needs to know where they are before they go inside.

subject: Timelapse — people moving through the space
reason: The {item} holds still for the length of it; the power bank keeps it running.

subject: Arriving — the train, ferry or road that brings you in
reason: An arrival tells the viewer where they are before a word is said.

subject: A sign or map that names the place
reason: One insert saves a sentence of explanation later.

subject: Low morning light raking across a table or sill
reason: Low sun pulls texture out of everything — and half an hour after sunrise it's gone.

subject: Food being made — hands, heat, steam
reason: Cooking is a sequence that edits itself: prep, heat, plate.

subject: People passing close through the frame
reason: Let a stranger wipe past the lens — it hands the editor a cut for free.

subject: Whatever's making the sound — bells, water, a kettle
reason: In a silent cut the sound carries the edit, so shoot the thing you can hear.

subject: Lamps coming on in the blue hour
reason: For about twenty minutes after sunset the sky and the street lights balance.

subject: Rain on glass, the street soft behind it
reason: Rain turns a bad-weather day into a mood. Focus on the drops, let the street blur.

subject: Feet on the path — steps, sand, cobbles
reason: A face-free way to put you in the place, and it cuts between anything.

subject: Over your shoulder, looking at the view
reason: Shows what you saw and that you were there, without needing your face.

subject: One last look back at the place
reason: An ending the viewer feels before they're told it's over.

subject: A long, still wide — let the place move inside it
reason: Hold for ten seconds without moving. Every editor runs short of these.

subject: To camera, close — where you are and why
reason: No mic packed, so stand an arm's length from the camera with your back to the wind.

subject: Sign-off to camera — one line on how it went
reason: Record it on the day, while it's true. It's the line you'll want in the edit.

subject: Talking while walking, camera at arm's length
reason: Keeps the energy up between the set pieces. Hold the lens just above eye line.

subject: Thirty seconds of room tone — nobody talking
reason: The editor needs it to smooth every cut in the interview. Record it before you pack up.

subject: The interview set-up, wide — them, the chair, the room
reason: Shows where the conversation happens before anyone speaks.

subject: Their hands while they talk
reason: Covers an edit point without cutting away from them.

subject: Them listening, before they answer
reason: A quiet beat you can drop in anywhere to shorten an answer.

subject: The day starting — lights on, doors open
reason: Starting on the routine lets the story begin before anyone explains it.

subject: The tools of the job, laid out
reason: The tools say what the work is without anyone saying it.

subject: An object that matters to them
reason: Ask what they'd save in a fire, then shoot that.

subject: Them heading home at the end of the day
reason: The day closing is the simplest ending there is.

subject: Opening the packaging
reason: The first touch of the product is the moment people remember.

subject: The product where it lives — shelf, counter, bag
reason: Context sells it better than a clean background does.

subject: A flat lay from straight above
reason: Stand on a chair and shoot straight down, in even daylight — no hard shadows.

subject: Someone enjoying it — the first sip, the first bite
reason: The reaction is the proof. Shoot a few and keep the unposed one.

subject: The shopfront, sign readable
reason: Clients always ask for the sign. Get it straight on and in focus.

subject: The room before anyone arrives
reason: The empty room is the before shot everything else cuts against.

subject: The details someone spent hours on — flowers, cards, lights
reason: Whoever organised it will look for these first.

subject: The speech or toast — then the room reacting
reason: Shoot the speaker, then turn round for the room. The reactions make the speech.

subject: Faces in the crowd, reacting
reason: Wait for the laugh, not the pose.

subject: The last people leaving, lights going down
reason: The room emptying is the ending events rarely get.

subject: Each step from above — hands in frame, nothing else
reason: Straight down reads clearest for a how-to. Keep the frame still between steps.

subject: The finished result, turned slowly
reason: The payoff of a how-to is seeing it done. Give it five slow seconds.

subject: Everything you need, laid out before you start
reason: Viewers pause here to check they've got it all. Make it readable.

subject: A slow walk in towards something
reason: Voice-over needs shots that breathe. Walk in slowly for eight seconds, knees soft.

subject: The master — the whole scene in one wide take
reason: Shoot the whole scene wide first, then go in for coverage.

subject: Over-the-shoulder reverse on the same scene
reason: Match the master's eyeline, or the cut won't land.

subject: An insert of the prop the scene turns on
reason: The script leans on it, so the edit will need it close.

subject: Timelapse — the sun going down
reason: The {item} holds the frame for the twenty minutes a sunset needs.

fallback.subject: Thirty still seconds on the sunset
fallback.reason: No tripod packed — brace on a wall or a railing and hold thirty seconds.

subject: The room with nothing happening — twenty seconds of it
reason: Locked off on the {item}: twenty seconds of the room at rest gives you room tone and a breath in the edit.

fallback.subject: Room tone, camera at rest
fallback.reason: No tripod packed — set it on the table edge and hold twenty seconds.

subject: Star lapse over the camp
reason: The {item} plus a power bank gives you the runtime for three hundred frames without touching a battery.

subject: A slow slide past something in the foreground
reason: The {item} moves the foreground against the background — depth you can't get standing still.

fallback.subject: A slow step sideways past something in the foreground
fallback.reason: No slider — hold the camera at your chest and take one slow sideways step.

subject: Inside after the light's gone — the room lit warm
reason: The {item} means you can keep shooting an hour after the light goes.

fallback.subject: Inside after dark, lit by the lamps already there
fallback.reason: No light packed — shoot by the practicals in the room and keep the lamp in frame.

subject: The product edge-lit against a dark background
reason: The {item} from behind and to one side draws the edge of the product out of the dark.

subject: People stacked up on a long street, the background pulled close
reason: The {item} squeezes the street so the far end sits right behind the near end.

subject: Them against a background gone soft
reason: The {item} wide open melts whatever's behind them, so the frame is only about them.

subject: Frost or dew on something close, before the sun reaches it
reason: The {item} is in the bag. Get under ten centimetres before the sun burns it off.

subject: One unbroken walk along the ridge or the street
reason: The {item} is packed — this is the shot it's for. Walk heel to toe and don't stop.

fallback.subject: The walk, in three short pieces
fallback.reason: No gimbal — break it into three short handheld moves and cut between them.

subject: Ordering at the counter
reason: You packed the {item}, so this can carry real dialogue instead of being silent B-roll.

subject: Hair or fabric in the wind, slowed right down
reason: Your {item} shoots fast enough to slow it right down. Put the sun behind it.

subject: Straight down from above — the pattern only the sky can see
reason: The {item} turns a car park or a beach into a pattern. Check the wind and the rules before you fly.

subject: The whole of a small room, from the corner
reason: The {item} gets the whole room from one corner. Keep it level or the walls lean in.

fallback.subject: The room from the doorway, then a second angle
fallback.reason: Nothing wide packed — stand in the doorway and take two angles to cover it.
